newsitem.title: USA: ConAgra to pay $8.3 mln to settle charges.
newsitem.headline: ConAgra to pay $8.3 mln to settle charges.

text.p: ConAgra Inc said Wednesday it agreed to pay $8.3 million to settle federal charges made against Peavey Co, a ConAgra independent operating company.

The company said it pleaded guilty in U.S. District Court in Indiana to charges related to mishandling of grain at 12 small and medium-size grain elevators in its southeast region over a four-year period ending in 1992. Peavey operates 76 U.S. elevators, it added.
Lynn Phares, vice president of corporate relations for ConAgra, said the charges "ranged from improper grading, misweighing and the application of inappropriate amounts of water to the grain."

"We regret the conduct at the facilities involved," Thomas Manuel, president and chief operating officer of ConAgra Trading and Processing Cos, said in a statement. "We offer no excuses, and we've made it very clear that we do not tolerate such conduct. No one charged in this case works for Peavey or ConAgra today."

ConAgra said it and Peavey have significantly increased control systems to decrease the likelihood of similar problems in the future. Additionally, Peavey has implemented compliance programs and training for all employees.
ConAgra said it also entered into a compliance agreement with the U.S. Department of Agriculture, which it said will result in no adverse administrative actions being taken against ConAgra.
The agreement requires the implementation of several compliance programs at grain elevators. Many of those programs are already in place.
Peavey is part of ConAgra Trading and Processing Companies, a division of ConAgra. ConAgra is a diversified food company.
